blocks.note: Nothing in this topology is accidental: the decision path and the audit path share one timeline in Data, Analytics & Lakehouse delivery, which keeps the blast radius of any change inside one lane.

items: FNOL packets, estimates and medical files arrived unstructured; triage queues held claims for days.
Straight-through rates below 20% on simple claims; adjusters spent time typing, not deciding.
Fraud signals arrived after settlement; SIU capacity wasted on low-value leads.

blocks.x: We deployed the claims decision pipeline: document intelligence (classification, extraction, validation) feeding Dataq Nexus decision policies with confidence-threshold routing, network fraud analytics scoring claims pre-settlement, and a portfolio lakehouse unifying exposure and claims for steering. Adjusters work a review queue of pre-assembled cases with citations.

The operating cadence, concretely: weeks 1–2 produce the signed baseline: current per 1,000 claims performance, method note, and a control owner who co-signs every later claim. from week 3 the working slice goes live at site scope: shadow first, then canary, then promoted cohorts — each promotion justified by the eval gate, not enthusiasm. What holds the build together is discipline at the boundaries: every state change is replayable from the signed baseline in Data, Analytics & Lakehouse delivery, which is what makes the reported delta defensible in audit..
